newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin again delays Pt Beach 2 restart.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin again delays Pt Beach 2 restart.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co again postponed the restart of its 485 megawatt (MW) Point Beach nuclear unit 2, and expected to restore the unit to service early April rather than March 5.
"That's been delayed to April 1," said a company spokeswoman, referring to the revised Point Beach 2 restart.
The spokeswoman said the company is still working with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission on a list of startup issues.
Point Beach unit 2 was taken off line in October for refueling and maintenance.
She added the unplanned outage of the adjacent 485 MW unit 1 this week contributed to the delay of unit 2.
"Unit 1's work diverted from work on unit 2," she said.
Wisconsin Electric shut Point Beach 1 Tuesday to repair a pump in the unit's support cooling system, which had a defect in the impeller.
"We're still working on the repairs. We also need to replace a service water pump," the spokeswoman said.
Point Beach 1 is expected to begin delivering power to the grid Sunday, she said.
The Point Beach units, in Two Rivers, Wis., account for about a fourth of the company's overall generating capacity.
Wisconsin Electric power is a subsidiary of Wisconsin Energy Corp.
